# Seven actual fibers: partial traces determine the global depth

This is an exact mixed-depth calculation in every continuous dimension
d>=2, with two integer coordinates. It shows that proper portions of
nonowned added fibers can determine the GLOBAL maximizing center and
the first-order maximum, not just the value at an unsuccessful candidate.
It also gives a counterexample to determining that first-order maximum
from added masses and conditional weak limits alone. It is not an OC
counterexample or a proof for arbitrary sources.

## 1. The source and its exact integer fibers

Let T be a d-simplex of volume V and centroid g, and let
Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, b0=1/(d+1), h=1-b0. Put T at the four bases
Q={0,1}^2. Add a convex body R subset T, of volume w>0, at

    r=(-1,0),

and the same convex body A subset T, of volume a>0, at each of

    p=(-1,1),  p'=(1,-1).

Two choices of A will be considered:

  (S) A=g+s(T-g), 0<s<=1; set theta=2Gamma.
  (B) A is centrally symmetric about g; set theta=1.

There is no centroid or shape condition on R beyond R subset T.
Let C be the convex hull of these seven lifted generators and let
mu be its actual mixed volume on Z^2 times R^d.

The base hull is the quadrilateral

    -1<=z_1<=1,  z_2<=1,  z_1+2z_2>=-1.

Its vertices, in cyclic order, are r,p',(1,1),p. Its integer points
are exactly Q union {r,p,p'}: checking z_1=-1,0,1 gives respectively
two, two, and three permitted integer z_2 values. The three added
bases are exposed. Explicit linear functionals uniquely maximized at
r,p,p' are, respectively,

    -2z_1-z_2,  -z_1+z_2,  z_1-2z_2.

Thus their actual fibers are exactly the assigned R,A,A. Every
continuous generator lies in T and every core generator equals T,
so every core fiber remains exactly T. No further integer fibers
exist, and C is a full-dimensional convex body. Its mixed mass is

    M=4V+w+2a.                                      (1)

## 2. A positive ordinary profile used in the proof

For a unit continuous normal u put B=u.g, ell=min_T u.x, and

    f(u)=|T intersect {u.x>=B}|/V,
    R_T(u)=|T intersect {u.x>=2B-ell}|/V,
    rho_d=min_u[f(u)-Gamma+R_T(u)].                  (2)

The proof in candidate 1d1be0b22c707856
shows rho_d>0: the expression is continuous and nonnegative, and at
each ordinary Grunbaum equality normal R_T=((d-1)/(d+1))^d>0.
Moreover rho_d<=((d-1)/(d+1))^d<Gamma<1/2. In dimension two it is
exactly 2(sqrt(10)-3)/9. Throughout assume

    a<=rho_d V,  w+theta a<=rho_d V.                 (3)

## 3. Exact depth of the nonanchor meeting point

At q=(0,0), the single actual point (q,g) has exact absolute depth

    A_mu((q,g))=Gamma V+w+theta a.                   (4)

Take any nonvertical through-point halfspace, with margin
u.(x-g)+beta.z>=0. If its r-fiber trace captures all R, that trace
pays w. Its traces in p and p' have opposite thresholds about u.g.
In case (S), the proved ordinary paired-centroid-tail inequality
pays at least 2Gamma a for these two traces together. In case (B),
central symmetry makes their sum exactly a, since a hyperplane has
zero d-volume. The own T trace always pays at least Gamma V.

If the r-trace does not capture all R, its threshold is greater than
ell, since R subset T. Its opposite core partner at (1,0) consequently
has threshold less than 2B-ell. The own trace and that partner alone
then pay at least

    [f(u)+R_T(u)]V >= (Gamma+rho_d)V
                  >= Gamma V+w+theta a.             (5)

These are two alternatives for ONE original ambient halfspace; no
trace has been optimized independently. A vertical through-point
halfspace contains the whole own T, whose volume V is larger than
the right side by (2)-(3). Tightening a containing halfspace parallel
to itself proves the lower bound for every closed containing cap.

For the matching upper bound let lambda_i be any barycentric
coordinate of T. The cap

    lambda_i(x)-h(z_1+z_2)>=b0                       (6)

captures Gamma V in q. It captures all R because z_1+z_2=-1 there,
lambda_i>=0, and h>b0. It captures Gamma a in EACH copy of A in
case (S), or a/2 in each in case (B), since both sums z_1+z_2
are zero. On the two adjacent core fibers its trace is a supporting
hyperplane lambda_i>=1, of zero d-volume; it misses the remaining
core fiber. This proves (4), including boundary cases in (6).

The same finite d+1 caps cover the whole q-fiber. At any y!=g in it,
choose lambda_i(y)>b0 and replace the right side of (6) by lambda_i(y).
The own T mass becomes strictly smaller than Gamma V, each A trace
has at most its previous mass, and R contributes at most w. Thus g
is the unique maximizer on the q-fiber, and every other point there
has depth strictly less than (4).

## 4. The global maximum and a genuine allocation transition

The exact global value is

    max_(y in S) A_mu(y)
       =Gamma V+max{a,w+theta a}.                   (7)

To prove this, the two other anchors (0,1) and (1,0) each have
absolute depth at least Gamma V+a at their own simplex centroid.
This follows from the contained-endpoint profile proof: their owned
addition and its opposite T partner form the triple A,T,T, and
a<=rho_d V. The other fibers only add mass.

There are matching isolating caps. For the two anchors use,
respectively, the nonnegative-on-other-core affine functions

    delta_01=z_1+2(1-z_2),
    delta_10=1-z_1+z_2.

Each is zero at its anchor, equals -1 at its owned A, and is at
least one at every other base. Therefore
lambda_i(x)-2delta>=b0 has mass Gamma V+a and isolates the desired
core cap together with its entire owned A. These caps cover their
own fibers. Raising the threshold at a noncentroid point strictly
decreases the own T cap and cannot increase any other trace. Hence
each anchor's unique maximizing point is its centroid.

The core (1,1) is isolated by delta=2-z_1-z_2 and has maximum Gamma V.
Each added base has an exposed vertical cap of mass w or a. By (2)-(3)
these masses are below Gamma V. Combined with (4) and the finite
covers just given, this proves (7) on EVERY actual source point.

In case (S), if w>(1-2Gamma)a, the unique global maximizer is ((0,0),g).
If w<(1-2Gamma)a, exactly the two other anchor centroids maximize.
At equality exactly these three centroids maximize. In case (B),
w>0 implies the unique global maximizer is always ((0,0),g).
Normalization is by M in (1), with no continuous-volume substitution.

For example w=a in case (S) gives the unique global maximum
Gamma V+(1+2Gamma)a. The largest mass owned by any single anchor
is only a, while the binary exposure cost at q is 2a: one must keep
its owned R and at least one of the opposite pair wholly. The exact
value lies strictly between Gamma V+a and Gamma V+2a for d>=2.
Thus proper traces matter in the GLOBAL optimum.

## 5. Conditional weak limits alone lose the first-order coefficient

Let tau=a/V tend to zero and set w=a. In the first family take all
three additions to be g+tau^(1/d)(T-g). In the second choose a fixed
centrally symmetric body about g, shrink it to volume tau V, and
use it for all three additions. For sufficiently small tau all added
bodies are inside T and (3) holds. Both families have exactly the
same integer support and fiber mass vector. On every added fiber,
its normalized probability measure tends weakly to delta_g.

Nevertheless their EXACT normalized maxima are respectively

    [Gamma+(1+2Gamma)tau]/[4+3tau],
    [Gamma+2tau]/[4+3tau].                           (8)

Their right derivatives at zero differ by (1-2Gamma)/4>0. Their
unnormalized first-order coefficients, in units V, are 1+2Gamma
and 2. These are global maxima at the SAME deterministic base and
continuous point, not merely two candidate-depth values. The
limiting atom g lies on each canonical centroid hyperplane, which
is exactly why a boundary-null hypothesis in a weak-limit formula
cannot be omitted.

This obstruction extends to every n>=2 by taking the Cartesian
product of C with [0,1]^(n-2) in additional integer coordinates.
For completeness, depth at a point in one binary copy equals its
original normalized depth divided by 2^(n-2). Restricting any cap
to that copy proves the lower inequality. Conversely every original
cap can be extended with a sufficiently large finite linear integer
tilt that exposes the chosen binary vertex and excludes all other
copies: the original cap margin is bounded on the compact source,
and the exposing integer functional has gap at least one. Taking
infima proves the matching upper inequality. Thus the same global
derivative discrepancy persists, scaled by 2^{-(n-2)}.

All fibers in this note have positive d-dimensional volume, so the
intrinsic measure is H_d and equals the finite fiber sum. Every
selected center belongs to an actual T fiber, and all ambient
halfspace orientations are handled in (4)-(5). The source obeys
OC with a strict local gain; no unrestricted conclusion is claimed.
